findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed that the facility did not have test strips for the quaternary ammonium sanitizer solution. CORRECTED: PIC was notified, left during the inspection to acquire test strips, and returned with test strips. Ensure test strips are available at all times for testing sanitizer concentration levels for all sanitizers types used in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
1ST REPEAT: Observed the following surfaces need maintenance attention:
(i) The 2x4s under the windows of the dry storage area/preparation area are unsealed. Seal any bare wood,
(ii) Several floor tiles that are observed damaged. Replace the damaged floor tiles. Placing a rubber mat over the floor tiles is fine for the interim for safety and cleaning, but tiles should still be repaired.
(iii) The wall paint by the mop sink at the mop station is peeling off and the wall needs to be repainted.
PIC was notified of these areas still needing additional maintenance. Ensure floors, walls, ceilings, and bare wood are sealed to prevent movement between walls and kitchen.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed a gasket in the back prep cooler is separating from the door, and could provide harborage for pathogens. PIC was notified and will get it repaired. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed to not use a barrier to turn off faucet after washing their hands. CORRECTED - The person-in-charge (PIC) was educated on proper handwashing procedure and the employee was instructed to wash their hands again. Ensure a barrier such as paper towel is used to turn off the faucet after handwashing in order to prevent re-contamination of clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: A crate of egg was observed to be stored above ready-to-eat foods in the standing cooler. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed and the eggs were moved to a different cooler. Ensure that raw foods are not stored about ready-to-eat foods to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas. [C]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: An Italian dressing that is produced in-house has been stored in the cooler for 3 days without the container being date marked after 24 hours. The PIC was educated on date marking sauces that are produced in-house and stored after 24 hours because it is a time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food. Ensure that TCS foods are date marked after 24 hours before storing in the refrigerator and discarded after 7 days. The inspector will follow-up on 02/09/2026 to ensure the facility is in compliance.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [PF]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Effective Pest Control: The facility has seen a sudden surge of pests related to outside source. Orkin has been called to complete a six month intensive service. The facility has several glue traps around the back storage area. Glue traps are observed to be filled with over a dozen pests of various life stages. The concern is being addressed, but the problem seems to be fairly extensive (all life stages observed). See violation #55 for maintenance items to address to support pest control. The facility is in good operating order in-terms of cleaning. Concerns to address are pest treatment and maintenance. The inspector will spot check the facility on 02/28/2026 to inspect pest activity.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.16 Exterior Walls and Roofs, Protective Barrier. Perimeter walls and roofs of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall effectively protect the establishment from the weather and the entry of insects, rodents, and other animals.  [C]

findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [PF]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The backup make-table cooler opposite the triple sink has accumulation of food debris. The PIC was informed and instructed to clean the cooler to sight and touch before the next routine inspection. Ensure coolers are kept free of food debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. The facility is managing a sudden pest problem. Traditionally, all these surface concerns would not be addressed, but when pests are involved, maintenance and cleaning are addressed in a more detailed manner. The recommendation of SCDPH is always to eliminate cardboard from the facility, acquire proper pest control (done), and work to insure walls are sealed to prevent movement between walls and kitchen. The following surfaces need maintenance attention:

1) The wall to the right (by the hand sink) as you enter the kitchen is pulled from the wall. See that wallboard is firmly secured to the wall.
2) There is a gap around the relief line from the grease trap into the wall. Use a foam caulking to eliminate this gap. 
3) There are multiple holes in the dry storage room ceiling and around the back door. Again, spray foam, cut flush will help eliminate gaps.
4) the corner trim to the left of the triple sink is damaged. Repair the damaged trim.
5) The 2x4s under the windows of the dry storage area/preparation area are unsealed. Seal any bare wood,
6) Walk around the back storage area and pull equipment away from the walls. Clean and secure cove base to the wall. There are several areas where there is gaping of cove base.
7) Finally, there are a few floor tiles that are observed damaged. Replace the damaged floor tiles. 
8) The wall paint by the mop sink at the mop station is peeling off and the wall needs to be repainted.

Now is a good time to address ongoing maintenance concerns in the facility. The building is old and Head West has been present for several decades. Revisiting painting and surface maintenance is appropriate at this time. 


(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed on two different occasions rinsing hands in the sink without proper soap or using a barrier to turn off faucet handles after washing hands. Discussed proper handwashing procedures with PIC. When washing hands, be sure to rinse hands first, then add soap and lather hands for at least 10-15 seconds, rinse, dry hands with a disposal towel, and turn off handles using paper towel before discarding.  Ensure that proper cleaning procedures are followed when washing hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed two boxes of single use cups in the basement. These cups were in cardboard boxes that had obviously been exposed to water and soil. The cups were discarded in the garbage out of an abundance of caution. According to staff, the basement had flooded. The inspector has been told on multiple occasions that there is nothing food related stored in the basement. Inspector became curious as to the storage of paper towels when the restrooms smelled heavily of mold and the paper towels at the kitchen hand sink also smelled of mold. Inspector noted boxes of cups with evidence of water damage when in the basement. When asked the staff stated that yes the paper towels had been stored in the basement. Three rolls of moldy smelling paper towels were removed from the facility and placed into the garbage. These towels were likely contaminated by water, the source of which is questionable and is not drinking water quality.

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that a home made type of sanitizer wiping cloths were being used in the facility. The cloths were made with quaternary ammonia based sanitizer. The facility does not have test strips for the sanitizer. The sanitizer was discarded and a fresh bucket of chlorine water was made at 100ppm. Facility has test strips for chlorine and uses chlorine in the 3 part sink. The violation is considered corrected on site. Provide test strips for Quat if product is to be used in the facility. 

4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

There is no CFPM (certified food protection manager) in charge at the location today. Employ enough CFPM personnel to cover all shifts at the facilities. When asked about the manager certification, the manager present said that she is ready to take the exam.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. 

The unit was not removed from the facility but it is not in use at this time. The unit will be unplugged. The facility owner is going to order a new unit for the facility. Until that time they will deliver food daily and use the make table only. The make table will likely not be able to cool all of the hot food and maintain the other food at proper temperature while bringing the hot food down to temperature at a safe rate. Inspector highly suggests operating as a medium risk and discarding any hot leftovers at the end of the day rather than cooling in the holding equipment.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. 

The cold holding unit for back stock is not capable of /does not have the capacity to hold food at 41F or below at time of inspection.
Inspector spoke with Grace at time of inspection by telephone. She stated that they have cleaned the condenser and cycled the unit on and off. They have been keeping temp logs but the food that was placed in the unit yesterday to thaw is reading 43F when probed with a thermometer during the inspection today. The food was moved to the make table (reach in part.) The unit that is not holding temperature must be removed from the facility and repaired or replaced The external thermometer reads 46F and the hanging/internal thermometer at the back of the unit is reading 41F. The back is considered the colder part of the unit and not the warmest part of the unit.

findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 
Food inside of the single door back stock cooler at the facility is 47F Roast Beef (middle shelf) and 49F Ham (bottom shelf). The unit is unable to maintain food at 41F or below as required by code. The foods were weighed and discarded in the garbage.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

Two priority and one priority foundation items were observed out of compliance during the inspection. Hand washing and temperature control measures were discussed with PIC during the inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed two employees to wash hands and then turn off faucet with bare hands. One employee was coached immediately and one was observed to wash hands a second time properly without coaching. Always properly wash hands in the food service hand sink.  Violation is considered corrected on site.

Food in the cold holding unit is between 53F and 55F when measured with a probe thermometer. The external thermometer reads 48F and the internal thermometer reads 47F. findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: The following food contact surfaces are soiled upon arrival: 1) can opener hanging on knives magnet 2) the soda nozzles. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use and any time they  may have become contaminated. The items were properly washed, rinsed and sanitized before the inspection concluded.  Remember that the soda nozzles are food contact surfaces and shall be treated as surfaces which need to be kept clean. Use gloves or clean barrier when putting them back onto the machine.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment: The single use drink lids are stored in a grey caddy with some dust and soil in the front edge. Also, some cardboard platter boxes are observed to be stored touching the floor in the dry storage area. 750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law. Clean the grey caddy. Boxes were moved to a top shelf.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment: Meat balls were between 120F and 140F at 11:30am. The meat balls had been on the steam table since 9:15am 750-210  Potentially hazardous foods shall be reheated rapidly to 165°F or higher through out the product. Properly reheat food to 165°F or above. The meat balls were discarded in the garbage. The meat balls were a reheat, The meat balls could be broken down into smaller portions to heat  quickly, more water could be added to the steam table and stirring during the re-heating process is important to get the food to re-heat in the proper amount of time.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.comment: The manager had a bracelet and a hair tie on her wrist and a ring on her finger at the time of inspection. The tails of the bracelet were observed to touch the tops of many loaves of bread, and drag over food including mayonnaise, ham and turkey. 750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination. The bracelet, ring  and hair tie were removed and her hands and wrists were washed.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: Wet cloth used for wiping is observed to hand over the edge of the sanitizer bucket. 750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses. Put cloth into water and store properly.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: The edges of the cutting board are observed to have dark score marks in them. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use. Sand and clean the cutting board for the make table so that no score marks remain to hold soil.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Container with veggie turkey has corner cracked off.  750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition. Replace container with one that is not cracked and is easily cleansable.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment: Phone and purse observed on prep table. 750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings. Do not place personal belongings on areas where food preparation takes place.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment: The prep table has an air temperature of 60F. And food in the table is above 41F. 750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below. Repair table to maintain food at 41F or below.

Provide properly constructed and clean floors. Replace floor tiles so that the area can be cleaned.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed pepperoni and Italian dressing that is homemade to have no date.  Dates were placed on these items to correct the violation.  Once items are dated the facility has seven days to use or discard the food.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
